title: El remedio
goal: Be sold a remedy for something you did not know you had
culture: The herb stall is where a great many people get their medicine, and a fair amount of it works. You are not being taken in. Say which part of you hurts, take the instructions seriously, and when she says no cuesta nada she is giving you something.

beats.es: ¿Qué anda buscando, mi hijo? Aquí hay para todo.
beats.good: Name the part of you that hurts. That is the whole consultation, and she will put the plant for it in your hand.

beats.es: Ah, eso es el hombre grande. Amarguísimo, pero le quita todo.
beats.good: Nearly everything on this stall is a tea, and asking is how you avoid a week of chewing bark. Hombre grande really is that bitter.

beats.es: Lo hierve y se lo toma en ayunas, tres días.
beats.objective: Say it back so you have it
beats.en: On an empty stomach. Three days.
beats.good: En ayunas is before you have eaten anything at all. Repeating the instruction back matters more here than it does at a pharmacy, because there is no label.

beats.es: Y llévese esta ramita también. No cuesta nada.
beats.good: She is giving it to you. No cuesta nada ends the sale as a kindness, and the only right answer is to take it and say muy amable.
